opportunities.title: Data Analytics Essentials Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space! A learning circle is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment. Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field. In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to: transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel query data from a relational database using SQL improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau We will meet online every Thursday evening, September 24 - December 10, 6-7:30 PM (12 sessions). Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis. Learners who complete the course will be able to: earn a digital badge download a certificate of completion

opportunities.title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles! What You'll Learn This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover: Essential Prompting Skills : How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results. Everyday Work Tasks: Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more. Data & Presentations: How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data. Advanced Techniques: How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time. Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions. Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once for the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address. A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, Thursdays Oct. 8, 15, 22 and 29 from 6-8:30pm. Registration is a two-step process. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Introduction to 3D Printing
opportunities.description: Learn how 3D printers work and how you can print at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class includes hands-on instruction with Prusa Slicer, the software used to prepare your 3D object file for printing on a Prusa MK3S+ 3D printer. Note: Customers are no longer required to attend a mandatory 3D printing class prior to using a 3D printer at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class is for those who are interested in learning more about 3D printing and how to use the Prusa software. Registration is required. opportunities.title: Digital Painting II: Forms in Still Life
opportunities.description: In this advanced workshop participants will be taken step by step through creating a still life digital painting from a photo reference in Adobe Photoshop. We will be using a Wacom drawing tablet. The instructor will touch base on important art principles relating to form, that will be applied to painting in Adobe Photoshop. Prior experience with drawing tablets and Photoshop is required for this class. Though, we will briefly go over the user interface and various tools we will be using. If you are looking for an introduction class or an in depth look at the broader aspects of Photoshop please look out for our Digital Painting I: Introduction & Pen Control or Introduction to Photo Editing in Photoshop programs. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Parenting in the Digital Age: An Essential Guide to Fostering Healthy Online Habits
opportunities.description: Managing children's social media and AI usage often feels like a constant battle over restrictions. Parents frequently find themselves caught between enforcing rules and maintaining a positive, healthy relationship with their children. In this session, parents will: Understand the key online risks and platforms relevant to their children's age group Learn practical strategies and language to encourage healthy online habits and open dialogue at home Feel more confident supporting their children in becoming safe, responsible digital citizens Hosted by Kids Rights Canada .

opportunities.title: Excel Basics 2: Do More with your Data
opportunities.description: An introductory class on Microsoft Excel for beginners with little or no Excel experience. Build on your basic Microsoft Excel skills and learn to use Excel data effectively. In this second session, you will: Practice data entry and formatting Manipulate rows and columns Create and copy simple formulas Convert data to a Table then sort and filter Create your first chart Upon completion of this class, you will be able to get more from your data using tables, filters and charts. Prerequisites: Excel Basics Part 1 or equivalent knowledge. Basic mouse and keyboard skills required. Format: Hands-on with demonstrations No Registration Drop-ins welcome until capacity is reached.

opportunities.title: "Make It Heard" 2: Civic Problem-Solving & Digital Advocacy
opportunities.description: Every community has problems. This series gives you the tools to do something about them. Over three sessions you will define a real civic challenge in your neighbourhood, design a creative response, and build something: a digital campaign, a poster, a video pitch, or even a 3D-printed prototype that communicates your idea to the public. Come ready to think, build, and be heard. Arrive 30 minutes before or stay 30 minutes after the program for one-on-one consultations. This program is part of TPL's Innovator in Residence series focused on civic innovation. From October 5 to November 28, join programs, workshops and one-on-one consultations led by technology strategist Ismail Mohamud to learn how technology can help you create positive change in your community. Learn more at tpl.ca/iir . Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. opportunities.title: From Portfolio to Book
opportunities.description: Join us for an online special career series with the 2026 Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence , Elly MacKay! In this series, Elly will share insights into building a career in children’s book illustration, covering topics such as the journey to working as an illustrator, an overview of classic children’s books, portfolios, and colour. Details about each session follow: Thursday, October 8, 7pm: Becoming an Illustrator Elly MacKay shares her early and current work, her career path, and her process for creating miniature 3D worlds. Her talk also covers developing your style, illustration trends, and how to stand out. Thursday, October 15, 7pm: Looking at Picture Books Elly MacKay gives an overview of famous picture books, the various styles, what works, and how they’ve changed over the years. She looks at cover design, structure, page turns, and how visual storytelling and words work together. Thursday, October 22, 7pm: From Portfolio to Book Elly MacKay discusses portfolios and what to include, as well as working with agents and publishers. She also looks at what goes into creating your first picture book. Thursday, October 29, 7pm: Colour and Atmosphere Elly MacKay considers colour in picture books—how it can be used to strengthen a message, or to alter the mood. She looks at how illustrators have used colour in unconventional ways in their books. Workshops will be recorded and available for replay through Zoom until October 31, 2026. About Elly MacKay Elly MacKay is a children’s book author and illustrator and a paper artist. She studied printmaking and illustration at NSCAD University in Halifax and University of Canterbury in Christchurch. Elly creates miniature worlds with drawing, painting and cutting, and photographs them for illustrations in children’s books. She has more than 20 books published in Canada and the US, including The Enchanted Symphony by Julie Andrews and Emma Walton Hamilton, I Am a Meadow Mermaid and The Secret Fawn by Kallie George. Elly is both author and illustrator of Frostfire, In the Clouds and Red Sky at Night and others. She lives with her family in Owen Sound, Ontario. About the Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence Program The Illustrator in Residence program honours the memory of illustrator Joanne Fitzgerald (1956-2011), and is a joint program of IBBY Canada, Toronto Public Library, and the Young Family. Accessibility: TPL is committed to accessibility. If you are Deaf or have a disability and would like to request accommodation for this event, please contact accessibleservices@tpl.ca or 416-393-7099 at least three weeks prior to the event. opportunities.title: Coding with Python II
opportunities.description: Python is an open source programming language that is used for creating web applications, web content, mathematics and system scripting. In this course you will learn how python code works and given time to practice. In this second Python session we will leverage everything we learned about loops and blocks in part one to create our very own functions. We'll take a look at how to approach function design, how to allow users to enter data into functions through arguments, and how to get our functions to return results. We will also introduce some new data structures which, unlike variables, can hold more than one piece of data at a time. Registration is required. opportunities.title: Google AI Essentials: In Person Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization. This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz. By completing the specialization, you will learn: How AI works How to write effective prompts How to use generative AI tools responsibly How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm How to stay up to date with AI news After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions. No AI experience is required. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. opportunities.title: Google AI Essentials: In Person Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization. This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz. By completing the specialization, you will learn: How AI works How to write effective prompts How to use generative AI tools responsibly How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm How to stay up to date with AI news After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions. No AI experience is required. How to Join a Learning Circle: Register once on the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address . A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions in person at Northern District Library . Registration is a two-step procedure. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Archaeoastronomy: Stonehenge and All That
opportunities.description: Join us at the Yorkville Library for an Archaeoastronomy Lecture. Archaeoastronomy is the interdisciplinary study of how people in the past have understood the phenomena in the sky, how they used these phenomena, and what role the sky played in their cultures. Today, astronomy is considered to mean the scientific study of the universe, but it continues to connect, in so many other intriguing ways, with every aspect of cultures, including myth, religion, and the arts.

opportunities.title: Youth Hub: Button-Making
opportunities.description: Express yourself and show off your unique style! Join us in the Youth Hub to design and create your very own custom pin-back buttons . Bring your own printed photos, cut up old magazines from our recycled craft bin, or draw a completely original masterpiece by hand. We provide all the specialized tools. Pin back buttons have long been considered wearable art, serving as a tool for advocacy, identity, and personal expression . We will teach you how to condense complex ideas into snappy text and eye-catching circular graphics using digital tools like photoshop or traditional art materials. Teens will learn the mechanics of operating a manual button-press machine and leave with a collection of wearable art pieces to showcase their personal style or support a cause. This program is part of Youth Hub service. Youth Hubs are a welcoming place for teens after school and in the summer, where helpful staff are always available. Free, nutritious snacks are offered daily. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more.

opportunities.title: Civic Spotlight: Guest Talk & Community Activity
opportunities.description: We bring in a real civic innovator: an organizer, technologist, or advocate to share their story and take your questions. Then they lead a hands-on civic activity to get you thinking and collaborating. Every Civic Spotlight is different because every guest brings something new. Arrive 30 minutes before or stay 30 minutes after the program for one-on-one consultations. This program is part of TPL's Innovator in Residence series focused on civic innovation. From October 5 to November 28, join programs, workshops and one-on-one consultations led by technology strategist Ismail Mohamud to learn how technology can help you create positive change in your community. Learn more at tpl.ca/iir . Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Excel Basics 3: PivotTables & Conditional Formatting
opportunities.description: Build on your basic Microsoft Excel skills and learn to use Excel data effectively. In this third session, you will: Use Conditional Formatting to visualize data Explore the power of PivotTables for data summary and analysis Sort and filter the data in tables and using slicers Take home practice data to improve your new skills Upon completion of this class, you will be able to get more from your data using Pivot tables. Prerequisites: Excel Basics 1 and 2 or equivalent knowledge. Basic mouse and keyboard skills required. Format: Hands-on with demonstrations *Registration will open two weeks before the class. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Seniors E-Connect
opportunities.description: Seniors E-Connect matches older adults with a teen volunteer to provide tech help, under the guidance of library staff. Learn the basics of using computers, tablets and smartphones and popular websites and software. Seniors, please register. Drop-in may be allowed while there are enough volunteers available. If you're a teen between the ages of 13-17 and would like to learn more about becoming a Seniors E-Connect volunteer, visit the Seniors E-Connect Volunteering page or contact the branch. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Cornell
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!
opportunities.address: Cornell Branch, 3201 Bur Oak Avenue, Markham, Ontario, L6B 0T2

opportunities.title: Design Jam: Kids
opportunities.description: A fast-paced, fun session where young creators tackle a real community challenge through brainstorming, sketching, and creative thinking. There are no wrong answers, just ideas, energy, and collaboration. If time allows, you might even start building a simple version of your solution. Arrive 30 minutes before or stay 30 minutes after the program for one-on-one consultations. This program is part of TPL's Innovator in Residence series focused on civic innovation. From October 5 to November 28, join programs, workshops and one-on-one consultations led by technology strategist Ismail Mohamud to learn how technology can help you create positive change in your community. Learn more at tpl.ca/iir . Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.description: What are people actually building with AI, not in the news but in your city, by your neighbours? Join our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln , and members of the AI Tinkerers and the Human Feedback Foundation communities, for an afternoon of live demos and projects at the library. See what local builders are working on, ask questions, and get ideas for your own experiments. Real projects, real people, no product pitches. A window into what's possible when curious people get their hands on AI. CHANGE: No registration required. Drop-in program.

opportunities.description: Seniors E-Connect is an intergenerational program that pairs older adults with teen volunteers to provide one-on-one tech help, under the guidance of library staff. Learn the basics of using computers, tablets, smartphones, internet browsing, eBooks, streaming video, apps, and more . Get one-on-one support in a welcoming and friendly environment. Drop-ins welcome until capacity is reached. opportunities.description: Learn scratch coding and create a game. We’ll explore the fundamentals of block coding while completing a basic project. Parents must be able to log their child into the scratch account. Scratch account is NOT mandatory to participate. All materials will be provided. Registration is required and is limited to ages 8+.

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Join an activity station! Activities include 'Pin the Spider on the Web', Kapla blocks, K'nex, colouring sheets, worksheets, and board games! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Let's learn about the weather! Join us for a weather-themed science experiment and interactive, educational weather activities. PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.description: Join our G1-G2 level Tips and Fun with Math virtually, where students can sit comfortably at home while receiving classroom quality math deliverables, develop basic logic and arithmetic skills, a general understanding of geometry, and practice simple word problems! We see the importance of building a solid foundation for student’s early math knowledge, and aim to guide their development with useful tricks and joy! - U+ Tips and Fun with Math - a creative and logical solution. - Materials will be provided. Parents participation is not required. Please note these sessions are on a monthly basis (please sign up for each class to receive the link): - Oct 5 - Nov 2 - Dec 7

opportunities.title: STEM in Action - Engineering Activities: Civil
opportunities.description: Civil Engineering: Earthquake-Resistant Tower Challenge Does your child enjoy building, experimenting, and solving hands-on challenges? In this civil engineering-focused session, participants will work in small teams to design and construct a tower that can withstand simulated earthquake conditions. Using simple materials, students will explore how engineers design structures that are strong, stable, and resilient. Throughout the challenge, they will test, improve, and redesign their towers as they learn what makes a structure stand up to real-world forces. Learning Outcomes • Identify and apply basic engineering design principles such as stability, balance, and structural strength in a building challenge. • Build, test, and improve the design of a prototype Participants: Children aged 8 - 13 years old Note: Please sign up for each of the four sessions for your child(ren) to be able to attend all four unique sessions in this program series.

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Join an activity station! Activities include technology-themed worksheets and colouring sheets, Kapla blocks, and LEGO! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: Science program for Grades 4-6
opportunities.description: Is your child in Grades 4-6 and would like to explore the world of Science? This program focuses on inspiring children to explore the field of Science and each session will run according to the structure: Activity/Experiment - around 15-25 mins (including discussion about the activity) Independent Research using iPads - around 20 mins (research a Science topic) - for those registered for each week, the student will research a new topic each week Presentation of research topic to the group - around 15 mins The topics for each week is as follows: Session 1: Activity/Experiment - Spaghetti tower (items used: spaghetti, marshmallows) Session 2: Activity/Experiment - Rainbow milk (items used: whole milk, liquid dish soap, q-tips/cotton swabs, food colouring) Session 3: Activity/Experiment - Measuring Photosynthesis with Floating leaves (items used: baking soda, liquid soap, leaves etc). Session 4: Activity/Experiment - Balloon Powered Car (items used: balloons, coin wrappers, modeling clay etc). ** Topics are subject to change and if your child has any food allergies/allergies related to the items above, please send us an email** ** Please note: Participants must be in at least Grade 4 to join the program** This program is presented in partnership with Students4Students.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: Bringing STEM to Life: STEM Community Program
opportunities.description: Join k2i academy within the Lassonde School of Engineering at York University for our STEM community program designed for youth in Grades 4 – 6 . Participants will have the opportunity to explore science, technology, engineering, and mathematics through interactive activities, creative challenges, and hands-on problem solving. Designed to spark curiosity and build confidence, the program encourages participants to see themselves as creators, problem solvers, and future STEM innovators. Participants will: Explore and apply STEM concepts through hands-on activities. Develop problem-solving and critical-thinking skills by designing and testing solutions to real world problems. Note: Each workshop is unique, so participants can sign up for multiple workshops

opportunities.description: Drop in anytime between 11 AM and 12 PM for a fun-filled hour of STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Math) exploration! opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Create your cool project and then present your findings to everyone in our awesome Science Fair! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
